chief_complaint: Uncontrolled stage 2 hypertension and cardiometabolic risk in a 58-year-old man living with chronic HIV infection.
history_of_present_illness: The patient was diagnosed with HIV infection in 2003 and has been maintained on a boosted protease‑inhibitor regimen (lamivudine/tenofovir, darunavir, ritonavir). Obesity (BMI ≥ 30) has been present since 2000, and prediabetes was identified in 2008 (A1c 5.9%). Anemia was also noted in 2008. In 2018 he was diagnosed with obstructive sleep apnea syndrome, but no CPAP therapy is recorded. Blood pressure measurements most recently show a systolic of 159 mmHg and diastolic of 112 mmHg (stage 2 hypertension) with no antihypertensive medication documented. Socially, he transitioned from full‑time to part‑time employment in 2018, reports ongoing environmental violence, and experiences chronic stress. He has had limited outpatient follow‑up since 2019, suggesting gaps in routine chronic disease management.
past_medical_history: Appendectomy (1984). Prior full‑time employment (resolved 2018). Resolved social isolation (2018). Two resolved medication‑review reminders (2017, 2018). Lacerations of hand and other sites resolved in 2018.

active_medications.name: lamivudine 300 MG / tenofovir disoproxil fumarate 300 MG Oral Tablet
ritonavir 100 MG Oral Capsule
active_medications.purpose: Pharmacokinetic booster for darunavir in HIV treatment

social_determinants: Part‑time employment, reports of environmental violence, chronic stress, limited outpatient follow‑up, possible socioeconomic instability, education to high‑school level.
risk_factor_summary: Stage 2 hypertension (SBP 159/DBP 112), obesity (BMI unknown), prediabetes (A1c 5.9%), anemia, chronic HIV infection on tenofovir‑based ART (potential renal impact), obstructive sleep apnea, Charlson comorbidity index 1, moderate clinical complexity. No lipid panel, eGFR, smoking/alcohol use, or family history available.

data_quality_flags.issue: Missing current BMI; obesity noted but quantitative value absent.
Renal function not recorded; important given tenofovir exposure and hypertension.
Lipid panel missing; needed for ASCVD risk assessment.
No CPAP device or therapy recorded despite obstructive sleep apnea diagnosis.
No data on ART or antihypertensive adherence.
Family history of cardiovascular disease, diabetes, or kidney disease not provided.
Immunization records (influenza, pneumococcal, hepatitis B, COVID‑19) missing.
No documented screening for depression, anxiety, or PTSD despite high stress and violence exposure.
No iron studies, B12, folate, or reticulocyte count to determine anemia etiology.

clinical_impression: The patient is a middle‑aged man with chronic HIV infection who carries a high burden of modifiable cardiometabolic risk factors: uncontrolled stage 2 hypertension, obesity, prediabetes, and untreated obstructive sleep apnea. Anemia of unclear etiology and significant psychosocial stressors further complicate management. Gaps in routine monitoring (renal function, lipids, BMI) and lack of therapy for hypertension, dyslipidemia, and OSA suggest under‑addressed care, increasing risk for cardiovascular, renal, and metabolic complications.
